title: Pet-Theft Claims Need Public Records Before Public Outrage
excerpt: No arrest, seizure, verdict, or shipment record appears in this material. Honest campaigning needs named cases, dates, agencies, and source links before claiming stolen pets.
body_html:
No police seizure, court verdict, or intercepted shipment is documented here. That gap matters. Stolen companion animals would mean families losing trusted members, while illicit transport could expose animals, handlers, and communities to cruelty and disease. But outrage must stand on verified records, not invented scenes.

Evidence must carry the charge

Claims involving poison baits, stun weapons, wire nooses, forged quarantine certificates, stolen pets, or crowded transport require primary documentation: police agency, location, date, case status, quantity, and canonical source URL. None appears in this material. Publishing those details without records would harm credibility and could misidentify people or businesses.

Lawful activity, regulatory breaches, and criminal offenses need clear separation. A court judgment requires a named court and case record. An arrest is not a conviction. An administrative seizure is not proof of a syndicate. Public demands deserve stronger footing.

Health protection still demands precision

Rabies exposure generally occurs when infected saliva enters a bite, scratch, broken skin, or mucous membrane. Once clinical symptoms appear, rabies is virtually 100% fatal. After possible exposure, wash the wound with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes and seek urgent medical assessment. Post-exposure prophylaxis includes vaccination and, when indicated, rabies immunoglobulin or approved monoclonal antibodies. Properly cooked meat is not an established rabies transmission route. See WHO rabies guidance.

Household exposure incidents and commercial supply-chain risks are parallel biosecurity concerns, not automatically one causal chain. Vietnamese families, animal protectors, health workers, police, and local reform leaders deserve transparent records and effective enforcement.

Demand abolition with documented accountability

Sign SDE's petition calling for nationwide abolition by 2030. Add your name to a public demand for action—and follow campaign updates on how that demand reaches decision-makers. Sign the national petition.
